breakfast.name: Shakshuka (Eggs Poached in Spiced Tomato Sauce)
breakfast.description: A Middle Eastern and North African favorite now synonymous with Israeli breakfast - eggs gently poached in a rich, spiced tomato sauce with peppers and onions
ingredients: Fresh cilantro and parsley for garnish
instructions: Heat olive oil in large skillet over medium heat
Sauté diced onion, peppers, and garlic for 5 minutes until soft
Add crushed tomatoes, cumin, paprika, and red pepper flakes
Simmer sauce for 10-15 minutes until thickened
Create 4 wells in the sauce and crack eggs into each well
Cover and cook for 5-8 minutes until eggs are set to desired doneness
Garnish with fresh herbs
Serve with crusty bread for dipping
breakfast.notes: The sauce can be made ahead and reheated. Control egg doneness by cooking time - 5 minutes for runny yolks, 8 minutes for fully cooked
breakfast.fun_fact: Shakshuka is popular throughout North Africa and Middle East but was brought to Israel by Sephardic and Mizrahi Jewish families. Today it's practically the Israeli national breakfast

dinner.name: Shakshuka with Ground Beef (Spiced Eggs in Tomato Sauce)
dinner.description: Middle Eastern egg and beef dish - savory and satisfying dinner
ingredients: Fresh parsley and cilantro for garnish
instructions: Heat olive oil in large skillet over medium heat
Add diced onion and red pepper, cook 5 minutes until softened
Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute until fragrant
Add ground beef, breaking apart with spoon, cook until browned (5-7 minutes)
Drain excess fat if needed
Add crushed tomatoes and spices (cumin, paprika, coriander, cayenne)
Simmer 10 minutes to develop flavors
Season with salt and pepper to taste
Make 6 wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon
Crack one egg into each well
Cover skillet and simmer 8-10 minutes until eggs reach desired doneness
Eggs can be fully cooked or with runny yolks - personal preference
Garnish with fresh parsley and cilantro
Serve directly from skillet with crusty bread for dipping
dinner.notes: Sauce should be just simmering, not boiling, or eggs will toughen
dinner.fun_fact: Shakshuka is eaten throughout Middle East and North Africa with regional variations
